claim: Drosophila can flexibly categorize a given stimulus into different groups depending on the options available.
source: Rather than forming memories that strike a balance between specificity and generality, Drosophila can flexibly categorize a given stimulus into different groups depending on the options available.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a key finding of the study.

claim: Flexible categorization in neuronal activity and behavior depends on the order and identity of the perceived stimuli.
source: We show that flexible categorization in neuronal activity as well as behavior depends on the order and identity of the perceived stimuli.
evidence: This is stated as a main finding in the abstract.

claim: Making choices requires assigning options with subjective values that can be updated through learned experience.
source: Making such a choice requires assigning options with subjective values that can be updated through learned experience (Hare et al., 2011; Hunt et al., 2012; Glimcher and Fehr, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Storing and updating values for every potential option separately would be computationally taxing.
source: In such a framework, storing and updating values for every potential option separately would be computationally taxing (Seger and Miller, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: It is beneficial for the brain to maintain overlapping sensory representations to allow options to be grouped into categories based on sensory similarity.
source: Instead, it is beneficial for the brain to maintain overlapping sensory representations, which would allow options to be grouped downstream into categories based on sensory similarity and assigned with common values (Seger, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Category boundaries must be flexible to allow distinguishing between two options from the same category.
source: It is therefore essential in such a coding-scheme that category boundaries be flexible.
evidence: This is stated as a logical inference from the preceding discussion about categorization.

claim: Animals directly compare the values of available stimuli and use relative value signals to guide flexible categorization.
source: One prominent hypothesis suggests that animals directly compare the values of the available stimuli and make use of this relative value signal to guide flexible categorization (Itti and Koch, 2001; Carello and Krauzlis, 2004; Mysore and Knudsen, 2011; Mysore et al., 2011).
evidence: This hypothesis is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Olfactory learning in Drosophila takes place in the mushroom body.
source: Olfactory learning takes place in the mushroom body (MB), where odors are represented by sparse activity patterns of the 2000 intrinsic neurons termed Kenyon cells (KCs) (Turner et al., 2008; Murthy et al., 2008; Honegger et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Odors are represented by sparse activity patterns of approximately 2000 Kenyon cells in the mushroom body.
source: Olfactory learning takes place in the mushroom body (MB), where odors are represented by sparse activity patterns of the 2000 intrinsic neurons termed Kenyon cells (KCs) (Turner et al., 2008; Murthy et al., 2008; Honegger et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Chemically similar odors elicit partly overlapping patterns of activity in Kenyon cells.
source: Although different odor response patterns are largely uncorrelated, chemically similar odors can elicit partly overlapping patterns of activity (Campbell et al., 2013; Lin et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Sensory representations are converted into value-representing memory traces at the synapses between Kenyon cells and mushroom body output neurons.
source: These sensory representations are converted into value-representing memory traces that guide behavioral outputs downstream of the KCs, at the synapses that they form with MB output neurons (MBONs) (Aso et al., 2014b; Hige et al., 2015a; Owald et al., 2015; Villar et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: There are approximately 30 distinct mushroom body output neurons that form compartments integrating input from different subsets of Kenyon cells.
source: These ~30 distinct MBONs form compartments that integrate input from different subsets of KCs (Ito et al., 1998; Strausfeld et al., 2003; Lin et al., 2007; Tanaka et al., 2008; Aso et al., 2009; Aso et al., 2014a; Takemura et al., 2017; Li et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: KC-MBON synapses are plastic and primarily undergo depression as flies learn an olfactory association.
source: Furthermore, these synapses are plastic and primarily undergo depression as flies learn an olfactory association (Berry et al., 2018; Cohn et al., 2015; Hige et al., 2015a; Perisse et al., 2016; Séjourné et al., 2011; but see also Plaçais et al., 2013; Stahl et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Synaptic plasticity in the mushroom body is mediated by dopaminergic neurons that convey information about reward or punishment.
source: This plasticity is mediated by dopaminergic neurons (DANs) that convey information about reward or punishment and arborize in corresponding compartments as the MBONs forming a series of DAN-MBON modules (Aso et al., 2014a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The degree of overlap in KC response patterns drives the specificity of learning and resulting behavior.
source: The degree to which KC response patterns overlap has been shown to drive the specificity of learning and resulting behavior (Campbell et al., 2013; Lin et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: During learning, synapses from odor-activated Kenyon cells to specific MBONs are depressed.
source: During learning, synapses from odor-activated KCs to specific MBONs are depressed.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: A similar odor with an overlapping KC response pattern exhibits reduced synaptic drive onto the same MBONs.
source: A similar odor with an overlapping KC response pattern thus also exhibits a reduced synaptic drive onto the same MBONs (Hige et al., 2015a; Perisse et al., 2016; Berry et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Greater overlap in KC response patterns leads to more extensive depression of MBON activation and greater generalization.
source: The greater the overlap, the more extensive the depression of this other odor's activation of the MBONs, and the greater the generalization.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the established model of learning.

claim: When overlap in KC response patterns is low, downstream MBON activity is minimally affected and the animal discriminates between the two cues.
source: In contrast, when overlap is low, downstream MBON activity is minimally affected and the animal discriminates between the two cues.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the established model of learning.

claim: The existing model of mushroom body learning does not include a means for explicitly comparing between available options.
source: Although this model has a lot of explanatory power, it does not include a means for explicitly comparing between available options.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the current model.

claim: Flies can achieve high levels of performance for both discrimination and generalization tasks.
source: We observed that flies could achieve high levels of performance for both discrimination and generalization tasks and identified a single MB compartment capable of supporting both.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: A single mushroom body compartment is capable of supporting both discrimination and generalization tasks.
source: We observed that flies could achieve high levels of performance for both discrimination and generalization tasks and identified a single MB compartment capable of supporting both.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: MBON responses showed no measurable stimulus-specificity to simple pulses of two similar odors despite flies being able to distinguish them behaviorally.
source: Surprisingly, MBON responses in this compartment showed no measurable stimulus-specificity to simple pulses of the two similar odors we used, despite being able to distinguish them behaviorally.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: When odors were presented in sequence, MBON responses to similar odors were clearly distinct.
source: However, when we presented odors in sequence, one transitioning immediately into the other, similar to what flies experience in the behavioral task, we found that MBON responses to these odors were clearly distinct.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: MBON activity is modulated by a temporal comparison of the alternatives presented to the fly.
source: These findings show that MBON activity is modulated by a temporal comparison of the alternatives presented to the fly, allowing for switches in the categorization of odor stimuli.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: KC representations did not show categorization switching to either simple stimuli or transitions.
source: Importantly, KC representations did not show categorization switching to either simple stimuli or transitions suggesting the involvement of downstream mechanisms.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: Behavioral experiments showed that comparisons are made when stimuli are experienced close together in time.
source: Moreover, behavioral experiments showed that these comparisons are made when stimuli are experienced close together in time.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: The mushroom body circuit implements a comparison that augments small differences between overlapping sensory representations to guide flexible stimulus categorization.
source: These results show that the MB circuit implements a comparison, augmenting small differences between overlapping sensory representations to guide flexible stimulus categorization and choice behavior.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: Pentyl acetate and butyl acetate are chemically similar and elicit highly overlapping response patterns in the KC population.
source: PA and BA are chemically similar and elicit highly overlapping response patterns in the KC population (Campbell et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Ethyl lactate is chemically distinct from pentyl acetate and butyl acetate and elicits different KC response patterns.
source: EL is distinct, both chemically and in terms of KC response patterns.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from prior work.

claim: Flies with Chrimson driven by DAN PPL1-α3 showed significantly lower performance on hard discrimination compared to easy discrimination.
source: Significantly lower performance on the hard discrimination task with reinforcement to α3 (p=0.007, n=12).
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Flies with Chrimson driven by DAN PPL1-γ2α'1 showed no significant difference in performance on easy versus hard discrimination.
source: No significant difference in performance on easy versus hard discrimination with reinforcement to γ2α'1 (p=0.08, n=12 reciprocal experiments).
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption and shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Flies with reinforcement to α3 showed no significant difference in performance on generalization and easy discrimination.
source: No significant difference in performance on generalization and easy discrimination with reinforcement to α3 (p=0.84, n=12).
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption and shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Flies with reinforcement to γ2α'1 showed no significant difference in performance on generalization and easy discrimination.
source: No significant difference in performance on generalization and easy discrimination with reinforcement to γ2α'1 (p=0.89, n=12 unpaired control performance scores).
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption and shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Rescue of the dopamine biosynthesis pathway in DAN PPL1-γ2α'1 is sufficient for performance on the hard discrimination task.
source: Rescue of the dopamine biosynthesis pathway in DAN PPL1-γ2α'1 is sufficient for performance on the hard discrimination task (p=0.04, n=8).
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption and shown in Figure 1I.

claim: KC inputs to both γ2α'1 and α3 compartments contain enough information for discrimination between similar odors.
source: We started by evaluating whether the odor inputs to the γ2α'1 and α3 compartments carry enough information to discriminate between the two similar odors used in our behavior experiments.
evidence: This is stated as a research question that was addressed, with results showing decoder accuracies were high for all KC subtypes.

claim: Many of the same Kenyon cells respond to the two similar odors PA and BA, but representations do not completely overlap.
source: The trial-averaged response traces of individual KCs for each of the three subtypes showed that many of the same cells respond to the two similar odors (PA and BA), but representations did not completely overlap (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: KC responses to the dissimilar odor EL were very different from responses to PA and BA.
source: Responses were very different for the dissimilar odor, EL.
evidence: This is stated in the text describing Figure 2C.

claim: Similar odors elicited similar response strengths in individual KCs across all three KC subtypes.
source: Pooling cells across all imaged flies, we found that similar odors elicited similar response strengths in individual KCs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, γ KCs: r=0.74, p<0.001; α'/β' KCs: r=0.76, p<0.001 and α/β KCs: r=0.63, p<0.001).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical support and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Correlation coefficients for KC responses to dissimilar odors were lower and not significant.
source: Correlation coefficients were lower and were not significant for the dissimilar odors (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, γ KCs: r=0.04, p=0.60; α'/β' KCs: r=0.06, p=0.55 and α/β KCs: r=–0.04, p=0.77).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical support and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Decoder accuracies for the two similar odors were as high as for the dissimilar odor across all KC subtypes.
source: Decoder accuracies for the two similar odors were as high as they were for the dissimilar odor, across all KC subtypes (Figure 2E)(γ KCs: comparing accuracies for PA and EL p=0.06, BA-EL p=0.08, n=7 flies; α'/β' KCs: PA-EL p=0.13, BA-EL p=0.13, n=5 flies; α/β KCs: PA-EL p=0.63, BA-EL p=0.73, n=6 flies).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical support and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: After pairing, MBON-γ2α'1 responses to both the paired odor A and the unpaired similar odor A' were strongly depressed.
source: However, after pairing, MBON-γ2α'1 responses to A and A' were both strongly depressed (Figure 3D and E, p=0.001 for A and p=0.001 for A', n=11 flies).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical support and shown in Figures 3D and 3E.

claim: No difference in MBON-γ2α'1 response size was detected between the paired odor A and unpaired similar odor A' after training.
source: In fact we could not detect a difference in response size between the two, even though only one (A) had been paired with reinforcement (Figure 3F, p=0.77).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical support and shown in Figure 3F.

claim: MBON-γ2α'1 responses to the dissimilar odor B were not affected by pairing.
source: As expected, responses to the dissimilar odor (B) were not affected (p=0.18).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical support.

claim: The depression of MBON-γ2α'1 responses to A' seen in single pulses was not readily apparent in an A to A' transition.
source: Surprisingly, the depression of responses to A' seen in single pulses was not readily apparent in an A to A' transition (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: MBON-γ2α'1 responses to A' were similar to pre-pairing levels when A' was preceded by A, but not when the order was reversed.
source: Responses were similar to pre-pairing levels when A' was preceded by A, but not when the order was reversed (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: MBON-γ2α'1 responses to A' as the second pulse in a transition were not significantly different pre- and post-pairing.
source: Indeed, quantifying the size of the MBON response to the second pulse showed A' responses were not significantly different pre- and post-pairing (Figure 4C; p=0.376, n=13).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical support and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: MBON-γ2α'1 responses to A as the second pulse in a transition were significantly lower after pairing.
source: As expected, responses to A as the second pulse were significantly lower after pairing (Figure 4C; p<0.001, n=13).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical support and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: After training, MBON-γ2α'1 responses to A' as the second pulse were significantly larger than responses to A as the second pulse.
source: The contrast with the single odor pulse results is clearest when comparing responses to A versus A' as the second pulse in a transition, where A' responses were now significantly larger (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C p=0.004).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical support and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Control experiments where LED stimulation was omitted showed no significant differences in MBON-γ2α'1 responses pre- and post-mock pairing.
source: Control experiments where LED stimulation was omitted showed no significant differences pre- and post-mock pairing (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3A–C.

claim: Transitions selectively enhance the otherwise depressed MBON-γ2α'1 responses to the similar odor A'.
source: Additionally, when we examined responses to A-B and A'-B transitions before and after training, we saw no effect on responses to odor B, indicating that transitions selectively enhance the otherwise depressed responses to the similar odor A' (Figure 4—figure supplement 3D–F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3D–F.

claim: In MBON-α3, responses to the second odor in the transition were depressed for both transition orders after training.
source: Responses to the second odor in the transition were depressed for both transition orders (Figure 4F; A'-A, p<0.001, A-A', p<0.001, pooled n=14 PA-paired and n=12 BA-paired flies).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical support and shown in Figure 4F.

claim: MBON-α3 responses to the dissimilar odor B showed no significant depression after training.
source: As expected, responses to the dissimilar odor (B) showed no significant depression (p=0.48).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical support.

claim: MBON-α3 showed very little contrast at the transition point, and contrast was similarly low for either order of the transition.
source: With MBON-α3, we saw very little contrast at the transition point, and contrast was similarly low for either order of the transition (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E, P=0.86).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical support and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2E.

claim: KC activity patterns trained with logistic regression using isolated odor pulses did not reproduce MBON activity patterns for odor transitions.
source: To match the training procedure the flies experienced, we first trained the models using isolated odor pulses, and tested predictions for odor transition stimuli... In contrast to our observations of MBON activity, model outputs were not significantly different between the two transitions, and were low for both (Figure 5B), indicating that transition-evoked changes in the KC odor representations do not underlie the effects on MBON-γ2α'1 activity.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: All three KC subtypes could distinguish odor transitions when logistic regression models were trained using transition-evoked KC activity.
source: We found that all three KC subtypes could distinguish odor transitions when trained to do so (Figure 5C, p<0.001 for all KC subtypes).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical support and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Flies learn to discriminate when trained solely with isolated odor pulses, not with transitions.
source: By contrast flies learn to discriminate when trained solely with the isolated odor pulses.
evidence: This is stated as a contrast to the KC decoder results.

claim: Flies showed strong upwind displacement during the second pulse of an A-A' transition, which was significantly larger than during the reverse A'-A sequence.
source: We observed strong upwind displacement during the second pulse of an A-A' transition, which was significantly larger than during the reverse A'-A sequence (Figure 6B, C and F, p=0.004, n=12).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical support and shown in Figures 6B, C, and F.

claim: In interrupted transitions with a 25 s gap, responses to the second pulse were not significantly different depending on transition order.
source: In these interrupted transitions, responses to the second pulse were not significantly different depending on transition order (Figure 6 D, E and G, p=0.85, n=12 for A-gap-A', n=13 for A'-gap-A,), and showed a similar degree of upwind displacement to that evoked during the first pulse, as expected.
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical support and shown in Figures 6D, E, and G.

claim: Starting locations at the onset of the second odor pulse were not significantly different in any condition.
source: Note that starting locations at the onset of the second odor pulse were not significantly different in any condition, ruling out the possibility that flies go more upwind with the A-A' transition because they start from further downwind in the arena (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, n=12 for A-A', n=12 for A'-A, p=0.08 for direct; n=12 for A-gap-A', n=13 for A'-gap-A, p=0.39 for interrupted).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical support and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The increased upwind displacement during A-A' transitions does not come from a linear combination of the response to the end of the first odor pulse and the beginning of the second.
source: Additionally, we ruled out the possibility that the increased upwind displacement during such a transition comes from a linear combination of the response to the end of the first odor pulse and the beginning of the second (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C-G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C-G.

claim: Behavioral responses to A' are distinct only when it immediately follows the paired odor A.
source: These results show that behavioral responses to A' are distinct only when it immediately follows the paired odor A, matching the odor transition responses we observed in MBON-γ2α'1.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the behavioral experiments.

claim: A single memory trace formed via plasticity confined to γ2α'1 supports strong performance on both hard discrimination and generalization tasks.
source: These results show that a single memory trace formed via plasticity confined to γ2α'1 supports strong performance on the hard discrimination and generalization tasks.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the DTH-rescue experiments.

claim: The overlap in KC response patterns is not differentially distributed across different KC subtypes.
source: However, we found that all three major subtypes of KCs exhibit similar levels of overlap across our odor test set.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the KC imaging experiments.

claim: Odor representations in all three KC subtypes contain enough information for A-A' discrimination.
source: Furthermore, we found that odor representations in all three KC subtypes contain enough information for A-A' discrimination.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the decoder analysis.

claim: KC responses to odor transitions could not account for the odor-transition responses observed in MBON-γ2α'1.
source: Despite this, when we examined KC responses to odor transitions, we found that they could not account for the odor-transition responses we observed in MBON-γ2α'1.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the KC imaging and modeling experiments.

claim: MBON-α3 received more synaptic inputs from a greater number of KCs than MBON-γ2α'1.
source: However, contrary to theoretical expectations, of the two MBON types we studied MBON-α3 received more synaptic inputs from a greater number of KCs, however it was poorer at hard discrimination (MBON γ2α'1=2,959 synapses from 336 α'/β' KCs and 3773 synapses from 683 γ KCs per hemisphere; MBON α3=11,360 synapses from 888 α/β KCs per hemisphere; Clements et al., 2020; Li et al., 2020)
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to connectome data.

claim: Flies make a temporal comparison of inputs to determine how a stimulus is categorized.
source: Our work instead highlights the importance of comparisons in determining how a stimulus is categorized. In particular we observe that flies make a temporal comparison of inputs and identify the underlying neural implementation of comparison in the MB.
evidence: This is stated as a main conclusion from the study.

claim: Flexible categorization in Drosophila involves a mechanism at or downstream of the KC-MBON synapses modified during learning.
source: We suggest instead that flexible categorization in Drosophila involves a mechanism at or downstream of the KC-MBON synapses modified during learning.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: Recalling food reward associations from one MB compartment is gated by another MB compartment depending on whether the fly is hungry.
source: In Drosophila, recalling food reward associations from one MB compartment is gated by another MB compartment depending on whether or not the fly is hungry (Perisse et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Ongoing motor activity can affect dopaminergic inputs along the MB lobes.
source: Ongoing motor activity can also affect dopaminergic inputs along the MB lobes (Cohn et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Long-term memory allows for more generalization than short-term memory.
source: Experiments have shown that long-term memory allows for more generalization than short-term memory (Ichinose et al., 2015; König et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Flexible categorization manifests at or downstream of the sites of learning, the KC-MBON synapses.
source: Here we establish a few important constraints on a possible mechanism for flexible categorization in Drosophila: (i) it manifests at or downstream of the sites of learning, the KC >MBON synapses
evidence: This is stated as a constraint established by the study.

claim: Flexible categorization modifies responses to stimuli asymmetrically - in A to A' transitions and not the reverse.
source: Here we establish a few important constraints on a possible mechanism for flexible categorization in Drosophila: (i) it manifests at or downstream of the sites of learning, the KC >MBON synapses and (ii) it modifies responses to stimuli asymmetrically - in A to A' transitions and not the reverse.
evidence: This is stated as a constraint established by the study.

claim: Offset responses in MBONs can be potentiated, presumably due to the timing of reinforcement.
source: Offset responses in other MBONs can be potentiated (Vrontou et al., 2021), presumably due to the timing of reinforcement (Cohn et al., 2015; Handler et al., 2019)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Activity of the APL inhibitory neuron is reduced by training.
source: Activity of this inhibitory neuron is reduced by training (Zhou et al., 2019; Liu and Davis, 2009)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Inhibition at odor offset is a particularly prominent feature of the α'/β' KCs that are input to MBON-γ2α'1.
source: Inhibition at odor offset is a particularly prominent feature of the α'/β' KCs that are input to MBON-γ2α'1 (Inada et al., 2017)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Making fine-grained distinctions is easier when a temporal comparison is possible.
source: Making fine-grained distinctions is easier when a temporal comparison is possible, but when it is not, more generalized categorizations can be an adaptive default.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study.

claim: Flies received 10 cycles of training and were tested for memory 24 hours later for experiments with DAN PPL1-α3.
source: Flies received 10 cycles of training and were tested for memory 24 hours later. CsChrimson-mVenus driven in DAN PPL1-α3 by MB630B-Gal4.
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption for Figure 1D.

claim: Flies received three cycles of training and were tested for memory immediately after for experiments with DAN PPL1-γ2α'1.
source: Flies received three cycles of training and were tested for memory immediately after. CsChrimson-mVenus driven in DAN PPL1 γ2α'1 by MB296B-Gal4.
evidence: This is stated in the figure caption for Figure 1E.

claim: Contrast around the odor transition was significantly higher for A to A' transitions than the reverse after learning.
source: After learning, contrast around the odor transition was significantly higher for A to A' transitions than the reverse (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D; p=0.001).
evidence: This is stated in the text with statistical support and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2D.

claim: The mean upwind displacement after an A-A' transition was similar to that caused by optogenetic activation of MBON-γ2α'1 in the arena.
source: In fact, the mean upwind displacement after an A-A' transition was similar to that caused by optogenetic activation of MBON-γ2α'1 in the arena (unpublished communication - Y. Aso).
evidence: This is stated in the text with reference to unpublished data.

claim: Flies compare available alternatives 'side-by-side' in time and stimulus history is important for flexible categorization and behavior.
source: Overall, these results show that flies compare available alternatives 'side-by-side' in time and that stimulus history is important for flexible categorization and behavior.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the behavioral experiments.

claim: When the two odors are encountered separately, both MBON-γ2α'1 output and fly behavior are indistinguishable for the two similar odors.
source: When the two odors are encountered separately, both MBON-γ2α'1 output and fly behavior are indistinguishable for the two similar odors.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study.

claim: When similar odors are closely apposed in time, MBON-γ2α'1 activity is enhanced and flies are attracted to A'.
source: However, when they are closely apposed in time, MBON-γ2α'1 activity is enhanced and flies are attracted to A'.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study.

claim: Learning-related synaptic plasticity resulted in depressed neuronal responses to both similar odors when presented in isolation, consistent with strong behavioral generalization.
source: Learning-related synaptic plasticity resulted in depressed neuronal responses to both similar odors when presented in isolation, consistent with strong behavioral generalization.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of findings in the Discussion.

claim: When odors were presented sequentially as at an odor boundary, neuronal responses to A and A' were distinct.
source: However, when the odors were presented sequentially, as at an odor boundary, neuronal responses to A and A' were distinct.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of findings in the Discussion.

claim: Behavioral experiments with carefully timed odor delivery showed that flies' response to A' was distinct from A only if they were delivered in a transition.
source: Moreover, behavioral experiments with carefully timed odor delivery showed that flies' response to A' was distinct from A only if they were delivered in a transition.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of findings in the Discussion.

claim: An odor boundary presents an opportunity to compare stimuli, and this comparison modulates memory traces by amplifying small differences between stimuli to change categorization and behavior.
source: An odor boundary presents an opportunity to compare stimuli, and this comparison modulates memory traces by amplifying small differences between stimuli to change categorization and behavior.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion.
